report.source: SciFact Wadden et al.2020;claims/annotations CC BY4.0,abstracts ODC-By1.0

protocol.features: FNV1a32 unsigned modulo128,log1p bucket counts,L2 per query/context block;concatenate256
protocol.response: support or contradict letters plus EOS;greedy,not forced valid verbalizer
protocol.policy: nonempty packed source,exact quotes,valid EOS word,first-token confidence>=threshold;output always unverified hypothesis
protocol.roles: 505 train/188 annotated dev,previously observed;no fresh confirmation
protocol.loss: teacher-forced response-only legal-token CE,ignore right PAD,mean valid tokens

limits: Small task-specific decoder is not a pretrained LLM,chatbot,free-form answer generator or scientific verifier.
Quotes are copied source provenance,not generated evidence or entailment proof.
Gold rationales/labels enter targets or diagnostics only,not retrieval,context features or runtime gate.
Query-only and cyclic mismatched-context are frozen-model controls,not separately trained fair-budget baselines or causal proof.
Rationale hit for controls records the original retrieved pack,not rotated decoder input;joint hit is a descriptive original-pack diagnostic.
Missing annotations excluded,not labeled false/unanswerable. Already observed roles,shared sources and2 exact full-role repeated claims limit independence.
First-token max confidence is uncalibrated,not sequence correctness or truth probability;thresholds not selected on diagnostic data.
No latency/hardware benchmark,prompt-injection resistance,clinical use or generative factuality certification.

One patient had preeclamptic liver rupture requiring liver transplantation. In 6 other patients, causes of severe liver dysfunction unrelated to pregnancy were found.

samples.text: 40mg/day dosage of folic acid and 2mg/day dosage of vitamin B12 does not affect chronic kidney disease (CKD) progression.

retrieved.context:
The aim of this study was the long-term retrospective analysis of chronic kidney disease (CKD) progression in children, especially with regard to the presence of hypertension (HTN). The average rate of progression of CKD was higher in patients with HTN than without HTN.
RESULTS Median serum homocysteine level decreased with increasing folic acid dosage, to a maximum at 0.8 mg of folic acid per day, when the homocysteine reduction (placebo adjusted) was 2.7 micromol/L (23%), similar to the known effect of folic acid dosages of 1 mg/d and above. The higher a person's initial serum homocysteine level, the greater was the response to folic acid, but there were statistically significant reductions regardless of the initial level.
CKD is an important risk factor for the development and ascertainment of AKI. Experimental data support the clinical observations and the bidirectional nature of the relationships between AKI and CKD.

samples.text: 1,000 genomes project enables mapping of genetic sequence variation consisting of rare variants with larger penetrance effects than common variants.

retrieved.context:
Genome-wide association studies have greatly improved our understanding of the genetic basis of disease risk. The fact that they tend not to identify more than a fraction of the specific causal loci has led to divergence of opinion over whether most of the variance is hidden as numerous rare variants of large effect or as common variants of very small effect.
Our results have implications for the detection and management of breast and ovarian cancer risk. More generally, these data provide new insights into the role of rare and of mosaic genetic variants in common conditions, and the use of sequencing in their identification.
We find that copy number and sequence can change in cancer genomes. Counterintuitively, human cancer genomes show a loss of copies, accompanied by global copy number co-variation.

samples.text: A high microerythrocyte count raises vulnerability to severe anemia in homozygous alpha (+)- thalassemia trait subjects.

retrieved.context:
Individuals homozygous for alpha(+)-thalassaemia have microcytosis and an increased erythrocyte count. Alpha(+)-thalassaemia homozygosity confers considerable protection against severe malaria, including severe malarial anaemia (SMA) (Hb concentration < 50 g/l), but does not influence parasite count.
Methodology: In total out of 850, 340 subjects with microcytic hypochromic anemia [MCV<80fl; MCH<27pg] from Southwest part of Iran, were studied in Research Center of Thalassemia and Hemoglobinopathies (RCTH) which is the only center working on hematology and oncology in Southwest (Khuzestan) region of Iran. These include 325 individuals: 171 with Beta-thalassemia trait, 88 with Alpha-thalassemia trait, 13 with thalassemia major, 11 with hemoglobin variants (HbS, HbC, and HbD Punjab ) and 42 with iron-deficiency anemia.
